newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, AGIP sign joint venture refinery deal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, AGIP sign joint venture refinery deal.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) said on Tuesday it had signed a deal with Agip SpA for a 50 percent share in the Italian firm's 300,000 barrels per day Milazzo refinery.

KPC also said in a statement sent to Reuters that its subsidiary, Kuwait Petroleum Italy, will acquire 330 Agip fuel stations in Italy with an annual throughput of about 500 million litres (110 million imperial gallons) -- 1.5 percent of the Italian retail market.

The statement did not give a value for the deal but said "the implementation of such an agreement is subject to the approval of (Italy's) Antitrust Authority which started examining this deal a few months ago.
"The agreement provides for a 50-50 joint venture which will own and manage the Milazzo refinery..." it added.
The deal would raise output from Kuwait's European refineries to about 250,000 bpd.
It allows KPC to "re-enter the Italian oil refinery industry and will expand its retail activity in Italy."
KPC closed its refinery in Naples in 1993 and has since been trying to re-enter the market in southern Europe.
The deal also provides for the upgrading of the refinery in Sicily to produce higher quality products.
